subject: humanities
passage: The Bayeux Tapestry, a cloth nearly 70 meters long, tells the story of the Norman conquest of England in 1066. Despite its famous name, it is not actually a tapestry. In a true tapestry, the picture is woven into the cloth as the cloth itself is being made. The images of the Bayeux work, however, were stitched with colored wool onto a finished piece of linen, which makes it an embroidery.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To describe the battle scenes pictured on the Bayeux Tapestry
choices.B: To argue that the Bayeux Tapestry should be given a new name
choices.C: To explain how tapestries were woven in England in the 1000s
choices.D: To explain why the Bayeux Tapestry's name does not accurately describe it

explanation.why: The key sentence is "Despite its famous name, it is not actually a tapestry." The rest of the text explains the difference between weaving a picture into cloth and stitching it onto finished cloth. The purpose is to show why the name is inaccurate.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text says the work tells the story of the Norman conquest but never describes any of its scenes.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text points out that the name is inaccurate but never says the work should be renamed. This claims more than the text does.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text defines a tapestry in general terms; it says nothing about weaving methods in England in the 1000s.
explanation.D: Correct. The text explains that the work was stitched onto finished linen, so it is an embroidery, not a tapestry.
